title: The orchestrator knows a writer's budget is the writer's own ceiling
description: run-agent-session.py starts a separate claude -p process with its own --budget-usd (executor.writerBudgetUsd); its spend is not drawn from the calling session's budget. Neither commands/run.md nor the drive's dispatch line says so, and a3e's orchestrator (cap 2.0, 1.84 left) refused to launch a writer printed with 2.4 and asked a human in a headless session.
desiredOutcome: An orchestrator following /audit:run or /audit:next launches the writer or reviewer session the drive prints without stopping to ask about money, because the printed step and the command doc both say the session's --budget-usd is that child process's own ceiling, separate from the orchestrator's

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "the dispatch line and its explain carry the sentence for both roles": a session dispatch made for a wave member never prints SESSION_BUDGET_RULE. walk_wave (drive-phase.py:4942-4955) collects each member's writer_said/reviewer_dispatch instruction and wave_said builds its print from only m["lines"][0] plus STEPS["dispatch-wave"]["rule"] (WAVE_RULE), so the second rule line added to the four STEPS entries is dropped, and the run: lines are still emitted through signal runs. An orchestrator driving a wave of writer sessions sees the large --budget-usd in the run: lines with no sentence under it, which is the exact situation the phase's desiredOutcome describes. sn4s only calls writer_said/validation_said directly, so no case reaches the wave path.
findings.resolution: fixed in P139.2-6sp (5536cf07004b): Have wave_said carry SESSION_BUDGET_RULE once when any member's signal has runs (or append each distinct member rule line after WAVE_RULE), and add a sn4 case that builds a wave of two session members and counts the sentence in the wave print and in its --explain.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause "and wherever else the dispatch is described to the orchestrator": commands/phase.md step 3 still says "`dispatch` -> a `run:` line under `--explain`: background Bash" and gets no budget sentence. /audit:phase is the entry that drives a whole phase, the longest run an orchestrator makes, and so the likeliest place for the stop. The executor's grep for the literal phrase "a writer's `dispatch` is a `run:` line" found four docs and missed this one because it words the same instruction differently. sn4d selects docs by that same phrase (tests/test_drive_phase.py describing=...), so phase.md is excluded by construction and a reword of the constant cannot be seen to leave it stale.
findings.resolution: fixed in P139.2-6sp (5536cf07004b): Add the same SESSION_BUDGET_RULE sentence to commands/phase.md step 3, and key sn4d on a broader selector (every commands/*.md that names a run: line from the drive, e.g. the substring "`run:` line"), so a doc worded differently is still pinned.

findings.issue: The sentence says the figure is set by executor.writerBudgetUsd, true for the reviewer and validation sessions only because reviewer_session_setting (drive-phase.py:1815-1823) copies the writer's budget and replaces only the model. An orchestrator reading a reviewer dispatch may look for a reviewer budget key that does not exist, and the sentence does not say that the same ceiling applies to each such session separately. Minor, not a stop reason by itself.
findings.resolution: fixed in P139.2-6sp (5536cf07004b): Optionally word it 'each session ... under its own --budget-usd (executor.writerBudgetUsd, the writer's key, also used for reviewer sessions)'; or leave as is.

findings.issue: P139-R1's resolution asked for a case that counts the sentence 'in the wave print and in its --explain'. sn4w counts SESSION_BUDGET_RULE only in w["lines"] from wave_said called directly; it never reaches walk_wave nor the explain text (render() joins said["lines"] into signal explain, drive-phase.py:8148 and :8300-8306), so the explain half rests on reading, not on a case.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.1 (d83aeee96039): Add one assertion that the explain text a wave signal keeps (w["signal"] via the same render/signal path) holds the sentence once for the sessions wave; or state in the case title that explain is derived from the same lines.

findings.issue: Two shortenings lose a gloss rather than an instruction. (a) The add heading and the argument it documents went from `--outcome "<what success looks like>"` to `--outcome "<..>"`: the placeholder no longer says what the operator writes there (the argument-hint line still says `<what success is>`, and add-phase --help prints the rest). (b) `Exit 3 (index lock held)` became `Exit 3 (lock held)`: it no longer names which lock, while audit-task.py documents exit 3 as the index lock held by a live run. Both leave the action unchanged (stop; ask before --takeover; pass an outcome), so no instruction is dropped.
findings.resolution: fixed in P148.5 (8e46457ccc23): If a few bytes can be found elsewhere in the run form, restore `index lock` (6 bytes) first, since it names the thing the exit refers to. Otherwise accept: the headroom is 8 bytes, so any restoration needs a matching cut.

review.outcome: [findings: 5 - 0 high, 2 med, 3 low; 5 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: The drive's writer and reviewer dispatch, and the command docs, say the child session's budget is its own ceiling
tasks.description: Where drive-phase.py prints the run-agent-session dispatch (the step line and its --explain rule) and in commands/run.md and commands/next.md (and wherever else the dispatch is described to the orchestrator), state the fact once from one source: the session runs as its own process under its own --budget-usd ceiling (executor.writerBudgetUsd), which is not taken from the calling session's budget, so the step is launched as printed. Name where the figure comes from. Cases: the dispatch line and its explain carry the sentence for both roles; the docs and the drive read it from one constant, so a reword cannot leave one stale.

add: tests/test_drive_phase.py: the writer and reviewer dispatch step says the session's --budget-usd is its own ceiling, read from one constant the command docs carry

outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: new constant SESSION_BUDGET_RULE ('The session is its own process under its own --budget-usd, set by executor.writerBudgetUsd; it is not drawn from this session's budget, so launch the run: line as printed.'), added as a second rule line to the four session dispatch steps (dispatch-writer, resume-writer, dispatch-reviewer-session, dispatch-validation) as a literal tuple (WRITER_RULE, SESSION_BUDGET_RULE) because _refs.followed_anchor_drift reads STEPS as a literal table and resolves names only inside tuples; the signal line is untouched, the sentence prints under the step line and so in --explain. The same sentence, verbatim, follows the 'run it in background Bash' sentence in commands/run.md, next.md, resume.md and review.md (the plan gate allowed the last two, which are outside the declared files but carry the identical dispatch description). tests/test_drive_phase.py (_signal_cases): sn4s counts the sentence in the lines of all four session dispatches (once each) and asserts the Agent dispatch-executor step does not carry it (the always-fires direction); sn4d derives every commands/*.md that says a writer's dispatch is a run: line, requires run.md and next.md among them, and counts the constant's text in each (whitespace-normalised) exactly once. Sweep of tests/test_drive_phase.py, test__refs.py, test__deps.py, test__help.py: exit 0, 4/4 files ok. wait-writer, wait-reviewer-session and wait-validation steps were left unchanged (they point at the same run: line but are not the dispatch). Dependants: tests/test_drive_phase.py - still correct, it is the file extended; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, README.md, docs/research/pipeline-cost-design.md - name drive-phase.py and its followed-step table, the README table row for WRITER_RULE steps still resolves (fa1 green, which caught my first draft); hooks/detect-plan-skip.py, record-risk-confirmation.py, stamp-verification.py, _areas.py - reference the script by basename or path only, no printed text changed except extra rule lines on four dispatch steps; names used elsewhere (_clip, _mark, _marked, _carries) untouched. Commands docs dependants: audit-task.py, tests/test__refs.py, test_audit_task.py, tools/measure-context.py (gate run, passes), PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md and docs/research/* cite the command docs by name and are still correct; plugins/audit/reference/verbs-in-full.md names next.md only.
outcome.descriptive: An orchestrator under its own budget cap is told, in the dispatch it is shown and in the four command docs, that the session's --budget-usd is that child process's own ceiling from executor.writerBudgetUsd, so it launches the printed run line without stopping to ask.
